result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=without, B=with): Both answers put the master controls and quiet hours at the top and group the toggles using their real names. B handles defaults for important versus marketing items more explicitly. However, B's 'Email updates' section groups by channel even though it says it groups by topic. It also claims the grid cuts 14 switches to 10 cells without support, labels a push pause 'Paused in quiet hours', and assumes the garden items are push-only. A is internally consistent, so it edges ahead despite a thinner treatment of defaults. | pass 2 (A=with, B=without): Both answers place all 14 toggles in sensible sections and put the master switches and quiet hours at the top. B's grouping is cleaner: its count of 3 global controls plus 11 topic toggles is correct, and it keeps the weekly summary apart from marketing. A puts the weekly summary with product news and sales, then contradicts itself by also hiding marketing in a separate disclosure, and its claim that the grid cuts 14 switches to about 10 cells is confusing. A gives clearer default on/off guidance for marketing, while B explicitly calls frost alerts time-sensitive and collapses news and offers by default, so the two are roughly even on that point.
